controlled_terms.definition: A comma or actual line-feed character separating adjacent Integer Tokens in a Number List. Custom delimiters are outside the current Product Goal.
Review by people who accept the Specification, Authority, planning artifacts, evidence, and delivered release.
A decimal integer written with ASCII digits and an optional leading minus sign, without whitespace or a leading plus sign. Leading zeros do not change its value, and negative zero represents zero.
Text that is neither empty nor a valid Number List. Its handling is outside the current Product Goal and must not acquire stable promised behavior in this release.
The result when a Number List contains values below zero. It reports every negative value in encounter order, including duplicates, using canonical decimal values without leading zeros.
Text containing zero or more Integer Tokens separated by Delimiters. An empty Number List represents zero.
Externally visible behavior exposed through the Python add operation or installed string-calculator command.
The identical local and hosted verification sequence: uv lock --check, uv run --frozen ruff check ., uv run --frozen ty check, and uv run --frozen pytest.
A calculator that accepts one Number List and returns its arithmetic sum. It is not an expression evaluator or formula engine.
Captured failing and passing public-contract test results showing incremental test-driven delivery without a prescribed commit cadence.

acceptance: Reviewers treat delivery evidence as part of the release outcome.
items.rationale: This assumption underpins the accepted Vision's problem and key benefit.
items.statement: The need for explicit requirements, TDD, verification, traceability, and human review is part of the product problem and value, not solely an internal development method.
items.title: Delivery practice is part of product value

acceptance: Project configuration declares Python 3.13 or newer.
Project setup and dependency operations use uv.
items.rationale: The implementation decision establishes the supported runtime and toolchain.
items.statement: The implementation MUST target Python 3.13 or newer and manage the project exclusively with uv.
items.title: Python and package-management baseline

acceptance: Any runtime dependency has a documented concrete justification.
Unjustified runtime dependencies are not added.
items.rationale: The release should remain small and bounded.
items.statement: The implementation SHOULD prefer the Python standard library and MAY add a runtime dependency only when a concrete requirement cannot reasonably be met without it.
items.title: Prefer standard library

acceptance: Empty input is valid.
Supported separators are comma and actual line feed.
The definition does not include custom Delimiters.
items.rationale: This defines the accepted input language.
items.statement: A Number List is either empty or one or more Integer Tokens separated by exactly one comma or actual line-feed Delimiter; comma and line-feed Delimiters may coexist.
items.title: Supported Number List

acceptance: ASCII decimal digits are supported.
An optional leading minus sign is supported.
Whitespace and a leading plus sign are not part of the promised contract.
items.rationale: The token grammar bounds the first release input contract.
items.statement: An Integer Token is ASCII decimal digits with an optional leading minus sign, with no whitespace and no leading plus sign.
items.title: Supported Integer Token

acceptance: Specification and tests do not assert stable outcomes for listed malformed forms.
Documentation identifies Malformed Input as outside the contract.
items.rationale: The accepted release is bounded around valid agreed integer-list use cases.

source_notes.text: Implementation decisions, testing decisions, and out-of-scope list.

items.statement: Malformed Input is outside the promised product contract; the product MUST NOT establish stable behavior or diagnostics for whitespace, a leading plus sign, adjacent or trailing Delimiters, a literal backslash followed by n, or missing or extra command-line arguments.
items.title: Keep malformed input outside the contract

acceptance: There is no independent CLI calculation path.
items.rationale: This is the selected design for behavioral consistency.
items.statement: The CLI adapter delegates to the public add operation instead of duplicating parsing or calculation logic.
items.title: Use one shared calculation path

acceptance: Local and hosted commands are identical.
The gate includes lock verification, Ruff, ty, and pytest.
items.rationale: A common gate makes local and hosted evidence comparable.
items.statement: The same uv-based quality gate runs locally and in GitHub Actions, without typing suppressions.
items.title: Use a single uv quality gate

acceptance: The equivalent supported input returns 6.
items.rationale: This illustrates coexistence of supported Delimiters.
items.statement: A valid Number List such as 1,2 followed by an actual line feed and 3 is summed as 6.
items.title: Supported mixed-delimiter calculation

acceptance: The release supports the agreed integer-list behavior through Python and command-line interfaces.
The release includes repeatable verification and human-reviewable evidence of intent, incremental TDD, and ownership.
items.rationale: This is the accepted Product Goal.

source_notes.text: The primary specification defines the first-release scope and evidence expectations.

items.statement: Create a usable, verified, and bounded String Calculator release that serves software developers and delivery practitioners by supporting the agreed integer-list use cases and providing clear, human-reviewed evidence of product intent, incremental TDD, verification, and ownership.
items.title: Deliver a usable verified bounded String Calculator

acceptance: Requirements, implementation-facing interfaces, tests, verification evidence, and reviewed release intent can be traced.
Captured failing and passing public-contract test evidence demonstrates incremental TDD.
Human review can identify the verified commit and quality-gate results.
items.rationale: The accepted Vision identifies the delivery journey as a product differentiator and benefit.

source_notes.text: Accepted Vision differentiator and key benefit.
User stories and testing decisions require auditable delivery evidence.

items.statement: Deliver the calculator through explicit requirements, incremental public-contract TDD, verification, traceability, and human-owned review rather than as an ad hoc exercise or finished-solution repository.
items.title: Provide a traceable delivery journey

acceptance: The symbol and signature are usable by a Python consumer.
items.rationale: This is the primary public seam.

source_notes.text: Implementation decision for the public package interface.

items.statement: The Python interface is the importable operation add(numbers: str) -> int exposed from the string_calculator package.
items.title: Python calculator interface

acceptance: The command is installed and invocable.
Supported success and rejection I/O contracts hold.
items.rationale: This is the secondary public seam.
items.statement: The command-line interface is the installed string-calculator command with one positional Number List argument and conventional stdout, stderr, and exit-status behavior defined by this specification.
items.title: Command-line calculator interface

acceptance: No requirement is added for capabilities outside the accepted first-release scope.
items.rationale: The release remains bounded around agreed integer-list use cases.
items.statement: Later String Calculator kata stages and unrelated product capabilities are excluded from this release.
items.title: Exclude later kata stages

acceptance: No custom-delimiter syntax is promised.
Values above 1000 are not ignored or treated specially.
items.rationale: These are explicitly outside the first-release scope.
items.statement: Custom Delimiters and special handling that ignores or assigns special meaning to values above 1000 are excluded; values above 1000 remain ordinary Integer Tokens.
items.title: Exclude custom delimiters and high-value special handling

acceptance: The release does not claim or require any listed capability.
items.rationale: These capabilities are unrelated to the bounded first release.
items.statement: Arithmetic expressions, general expression evaluation, additional calculator operations, web or graphical interfaces, persistence, accounts, networking, and services are excluded.
items.title: Exclude unrelated product capabilities

acceptance: This specification does not prescribe sprint duration, estimates, task breakdown, or implementation order.
items.rationale: AgileForge planning owns these decisions after Specification and Authority acceptance.
items.statement: Sprint duration, story-point capacity, task decomposition, and implementation sequencing are excluded from this Specification and remain planning concerns.
items.title: Exclude delivery planning decisions

acceptance: Before release acceptance, reviewers can locate and inspect the evidence.
The evidence names the exact verified commit and all gate results.
items.rationale: The specification requires evidence but does not prescribe its storage format.

source_notes.text: Testing decisions require evidence but do not prescribe an artifact location or format.

items.statement: The exact repository location and presentation format for captured failing and passing TDD evidence and completion quality-gate evidence remains to be selected during delivery, provided the evidence identifies the verified commit and results clearly.
items.title: Evidence artifact location and review format

acceptance: Public behavior is tested at public seams.
CLI output and status are deterministic for supported inputs.
items.rationale: The product serves developers and delivery practitioners and must support reliable use and review.

source_notes.text: Accepted Vision product category and benefit.

items.statement: The public Python and command-line contracts SHOULD remain small, predictable, externally verifiable, and suitable for automation.
items.title: Predictable public contract

acceptance: Importing add from string_calculator succeeds.
add accepts one string argument and returns an integer for supported input.
The public contract does not require consumers to import internal modules.
items.rationale: Python developers need a small stable public contract without depending on internal modules.

source_notes.text: User stories 1 and 2 and the implementation decisions define the public operation.

items.statement: The product MUST export a public Python operation add(numbers: str) -> int directly from the string_calculator package interface.
items.title: Expose the public Python operation

acceptance: add("") returns 0.
items.rationale: An empty Number List has an explicit product meaning.

source_notes.text: User story 3 and implementation decision for empty input.

items.statement: The Python operation MUST return zero for an empty Number List.
items.title: Return zero for empty input

acceptance: One non-negative Integer Token returns its numeric value.
Comma-separated tokens return their arithmetic sum.
Line-feed-separated tokens return their arithmetic sum.
Comma and line-feed Delimiters may coexist.
There is no arbitrary product-level maximum number of Integer Tokens.
items.rationale: Summation of integer lists is the core calculator behavior.

source_notes.text: User stories 4 through 8 and implementation decisions.

items.statement: The Python operation MUST sum one or more supported non-negative Integer Tokens separated by supported Delimiters.
items.title: Sum supported integer tokens

acceptance: A token such as 007 contributes 7.
A token such as -0 is accepted as zero.
Zero and leading-zero spellings produce their numeric meanings.
items.rationale: Equivalent decimal spellings must not change the sum or cause false negative rejection.

source_notes.text: User stories 9 and 10 and implementation decisions.

items.statement: The product MUST interpret leading-zero spellings by numeric value and MUST treat negative zero as zero.
items.title: Interpret integer token spelling numerically

acceptance: Any negative value causes ValueError.
No partial sum is returned when rejection occurs.
Negative zero does not cause rejection.
items.rationale: Negative input must never be mistaken for a successful partial calculation.

source_notes.text: User stories 11 through 14 and implementation decisions.

items.statement: The Python operation MUST reject the entire Number List when any parsed value is below zero by raising ValueError rather than returning a partial sum.
items.title: Reject all negative values

acceptance: The complete ValueError message equals `negative numbers not allowed: ` followed by the canonical negative values and nothing else.
Negative values appear in encounter order.
Repeated negative values remain repeated in the diagnostic.
Equivalent negative spellings are rendered as canonical decimal values without leading zeros.
Canonical negative values are separated by exactly comma and space.
items.rationale: The diagnostic is an exact public contract that lets users map every invalid occurrence back to the input without permitting additional prefix, suffix, or text.

source_notes.text: User stories 12 through 14 and implementation decisions require the exact rejection text, ordering, canonicalization, and duplicate preservation.

items.statement: For a Number List containing one or more negative values, the Python operation MUST raise ValueError whose complete message equals `negative numbers not allowed: ` followed only by every canonical negative value in encounter order, with duplicate occurrences preserved and values separated by comma and space.
items.title: Report every negative occurrence exactly

acceptance: The installed command is named string-calculator.
A supported Number List can be supplied as one positional argument.
Actual shell-quoted line feeds are accepted as Delimiters.
items.rationale: The release must be directly scriptable by command-line users.

source_notes.text: User stories 15 and 16 and implementation decisions.

items.statement: The product MUST install a string-calculator command accepting one supported Number List as a positional argument.
items.title: Provide the command-line interface

acceptance: Standard output contains only the decimal sum followed by one newline.
Standard error is empty.
The process exits with status zero.
items.rationale: Reliable output and status are required for automation.
items.statement: For a successful supported invocation, the command MUST write only the decimal sum and one trailing newline to standard output, write nothing to standard error, and exit zero.
items.title: Define successful CLI behavior

acceptance: Standard output contains no sum.
Standard error equals the Python ValueError message followed by exactly one trailing newline.
The process exits with a nonzero status.
items.rationale: Automation must distinguish rejection from a successful sum.

source_notes.text: User story 18 and implementation decisions preserve the exact Python error text and CLI stderr and trailing-newline behavior.

items.statement: For negative-number rejection, the command MUST write the exact Python error text and one trailing newline to standard error, write no sum to standard output, and exit nonzero.
items.title: Define negative CLI behavior

acceptance: CLI calculations are performed through add.
Public Python and CLI behavior remains governed by the same calculation implementation.
items.rationale: A shared calculation path prevents interface behavior drift.

source_notes.text: User story 19 and implementation decision for CLI delegation.

items.statement: The command-line adapter MUST delegate to the public add operation and MUST NOT implement an independent parser or calculation path.
items.title: Use one calculation path

acceptance: The primary test seam is public add.
The secondary seam is the installed command through subprocess tests.
Tests do not require internal helper or module structure.
items.rationale: Implementation details may change without invalidating the product contract.
items.statement: Tests MUST exercise externally visible behavior through the public Python add operation and the installed command rather than parser structure, helper calls, or module organization.
items.title: Test public behavior

acceptance: Each listed supported partition has public-contract coverage.
Negative rejection order and duplicate preservation are tested.
CLI tests cover successful output and status, actual line-feed handling, and negative standard-error and nonzero behavior without duplicating every Python case.
items.rationale: Acceptance must not depend on a few representative examples.
items.statement: The test suite MUST explicitly cover the supported behavior partitions, including empty input, one and many values, comma and line-feed Delimiters, mixed Delimiters, zero, leading zeros, negative zero, and negative rejection order and duplication.
items.title: Cover supported behavior partitions

acceptance: The four commands are present in the local quality gate.
The same four commands run in GitHub Actions.
The gate uses no typing suppressions.
items.rationale: Comparable evidence is needed for human review.
items.statement: Local verification and GitHub Actions MUST run the same quality gate: uv lock --check, uv run --frozen ruff check ., uv run --frozen ty check, and uv run --frozen pytest.
items.title: Provide comparable local and hosted verification

acceptance: Evidence identifies one exact commit SHA.
Evidence records successful results for every quality-gate command.
The evidence is available for human review.
items.rationale: The reviewed result must be unambiguous.
items.statement: Completion evidence MUST identify the exact verified commit and the successful quality-gate results.
items.title: Identify the verified release commit

acceptance: Captured evidence includes public-contract test failure before the corresponding behavior is implemented.
Captured evidence includes the subsequent passing result.
Evidence does not require a prescribed number or pattern of commits.
items.rationale: The claimed incremental TDD journey must be auditable while leaving implementation sequencing flexible.
items.statement: The release evidence MUST show visible failing and passing progression at public seams without requiring a particular commit cadence.
items.title: Capture incremental TDD evidence

acceptance: CLI delegation to add is inspected.
Both seams have contract tests.
items.rationale: The two public seams expose the same product behavior.

source_notes.text: Shared calculation-path decision and testing decisions.

items.statement: The Python and command-line interfaces could diverge if the CLI duplicates parsing or calculation behavior.
items.title: Interface behavior drift

acceptance: Failing and passing public-contract evidence is captured.
The verified commit and quality-gate results are recorded.
items.rationale: Evidence is an explicit product benefit and acceptance concern.

source_notes.text: Testing decisions and reviewer user stories.

items.statement: The release could be technically functional but fail to demonstrate the required traceable incremental TDD journey and human-owned review.
items.title: Insufficient TDD or release evidence

acceptance: Malformed forms are explicitly documented as outside the contract.
Tests do not establish stable malformed-input behavior.
items.rationale: Malformed Input is deliberately outside the Product Goal.

payload.problem_statement: Software developers need a usable, bounded String Calculator whose behavior is explicit and verifiable. Delivery practitioners also need clear evidence that the product moved from reviewed intent through incremental TDD, verification, and human-owned review. Ad hoc exercises and repositories containing finished solutions do not provide both the usable result and its traceable delivery journey.
